It came on fairly quickly over just a couple of weeks after that job change, and it's just dragged me down completely.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the sadness started about three months ago, fairly quickly after the job change, but can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt significantly better or back to your normal self during these three months?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I feel normal, but my mood swings to the complete opposite extreme sometimes. I'll suddenly get weirdly pumped up, full of energy, and feel like I'm on top of the world and don't even need sleep. But those high times can also make me really irritable and feel like I'm spinning out of control.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how often these extreme mood swings from deep sadness to feeling 'on top of the world' happen, and do they seem to follow any pattern or are they completely unpredictable?\n\nPatient: These extreme swings have been happening back and forth for the last three months, ever since my job was restructured. There’s really no pattern to it; it feels completely chaotic and unpredictable. I’ll just suddenly swing from being highly energetic and pumped up to crashing right back into that heavy, drained depression.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how long these episodes of feeling 'on top of the world' typically last, and do they always end with a crash back into depression, or are there times when you come back down to a more neutral mood?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days those high periods last, or if I ever truly reach a neutral middle ground. For the last three months, it has just felt like a constant, exhausting cycle of swinging between being intensely wound up and crashing straight back down into that heavy depression. There really isn't much of a break in between.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate the shortest and longest duration of these high-energy episodes, and do you notice any triggers that consistently precede the switch from a high to a low mood or vice versa?\n\nPatient: I'm honestly not sure how long those high-energy phases actually last, and I can't really tell you what triggers the switches between them. All I know is this whole roller coaster started right after the company restructuring, and it's just been chaotic ever since.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to give me a more specific idea of how long the episodes of feeling 'on top of the world' last, even if it's just a rough estimate, such as a few days, a week, or longer, to help me better understand your condition?\n\nPatient: Those wired, high-energy times usually last for several days at a time before I crash back down into the heavy depression. This whole back-and-forth has been happening on and off for the last three months since the job restructuring.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the periods of feeling 'on top of the world' and the periods of deep sadness both last for several days, or if one typically lasts longer than the other?\n\nPatient: I've definitely gone through both of those states over the last three months, but I'm really not sure which one lasts longer or how many days each one takes up. Ever since they changed my job around, everything has just felt like a giant, confusing blur.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to compare the duration of your high-energy episodes to your depressive episodes, do they seem to last roughly the same amount of time or does one tend to last longer than the other?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure how to compare the exact duration of the high-energy periods versus the down periods. Both of those states have just been cycling and happening on and off over the last three months since my job changed. It's all been such a blur that I can't tell which one lasts longer.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instance where you had a full week or more of consistent high-energy feelings without crashing back into depression, or has it always been shorter periods of highs followed by lows?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days. Over the last three months, I've had those intense 'up' periods where I felt wired and barely slept for days at a time, but I can't quite remember if a single high period lasted a full week straight before I crashed back down.\n\nDoctor: Can you recall any period during the last three months where you had at least two weeks of consistent mood, either high or low, without significant switching, to help clarify the pattern of your mood swings?\n\nPatient: That heavy, hopeless depression has actually been a constant, overriding feeling for the entire three months since my job changed. Even though I have those intense, wired 'up' periods, the deep sadness has been my most consistent baseline over this whole time.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have experienced at least one episode of abnormally elevated mood that lasted for most of the day for at least four consecutive days, or if the high-energy periods are always shorter?\n\nPatient: Yes, those pumped-up, high-energy periods definitely last for several days in a row, easily more than four days at a time. During those stretches, I feel like I'm driven by a motor, barely sleep, and am constantly on the go until I eventually crash. It's definitely not just a quick thing that lasts a few hours or a single day.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether your depressive episodes, the periods of deep sadness, have lasted for two weeks or more without interruption by one of your high-energy episodes?\n\nPatient: Yes, that heavy, hopeless depression has been weighing me down constantly for about three months now, ever since the work restructuring happened. It has basically been there the entire time, lasting way longer than two weeks without any real break from the sadness.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt consistently depressed without any significant improvement, and separately, have you had any periods of abnormally elevated mood lasting at least four consecutive days without switching back to depression?\n\nPatient: Yes, that heavy, hopeless depression has been constant for the entire three months since the restructuring, with absolutely no improvement. And separately, those high, wired periods have been happening on and off during those same three months, lasting for days at a time when they hit.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if the longest duration of your depressive episodes and the longest duration of your high-energy episodes have both lasted for more than two weeks, or has one consistently been shorter than the other?\n\nPatient: I know for sure that the heavy depression has been dragging me down for the entire three months. But I'm really not sure about the exact duration of those high-energy periods or how they compare in length to the down times.\n\nDoctor: Can you definitively say if you've had any single episode, either high or low, that lasted for more than two weeks without switching to the other state?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure about the exact timing or if I ever went a full two weeks in just one state without any of those other feelings creeping in. Everything has just felt like a chaotic blur of highs and lows over the last three months.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if there has been a period where you were consistently in a high-energy state or a depressive state for more than two weeks without any significant switch to the other state, to help clarify the pattern of your mood swings?\n\nPatient: The heavy, hopeless depression has definitely been there for about three months since they changed my job around. But it's hard to say it was completely uninterrupted because of those intense, sudden spikes of high energy and irritability that keep swinging back and forth during this same time.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least one episode of depression that lasted for two weeks or more without any significant improvement or switch to a high-energy state, and separately, if you've had any high-energy episode lasting more than two weeks without switching back to depression?\n\nPatient: The heavy, hopeless depression has definitely been dragging me down constantly for the last three months straight since my job changed. But those high-energy phases don't last for two weeks straight; they just pop up and swing back and forth with the crashes during that same three-month period.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any episodes of high energy that lasted more than two weeks without switching to depression, or do the high-energy episodes always last less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure about the exact duration of those high-energy phases or how many weeks they last individually. They just seem to come and go amidst the overall chaos of everything I've been going through over the last three months.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether the high-energy episodes typically last less than two weeks before switching back to depression, as this will help clarify the nature of your mood swings?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure exactly how many days or weeks those high phases last. All I can tell you is that I've been bouncing back and forth between those highs and lows over the last three months.\n\nDoctor: To clarify, do your high-energy episodes typically last less than two weeks before you switch back to feeling depressed, or is it possible for them to last longer than two weeks without switching?\n\nPatient: I'm really not entirely sure of the exact number of weeks those high-energy phases last. I just know that I've been swinging back and forth between those intense highs and heavy crashes over the past three months.\n\nDoctor: Can you definitively say whether your high-energy episodes always last less than two weeks before switching back to depression, which could help differentiate between possible conditions?"

It came on fairly quickly over just a couple of weeks after that job change, and it's just dragged me down completely.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the sadness started about three months ago, fairly quickly after the job change, but can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt significantly better or back to your normal self during these three months?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I feel normal, but my mood swings to the complete opposite extreme sometimes.
